records.label: spacr.timeflows_qc.recycled_labels#1
records.source: A recycled id -- the same number given to an unrelated object after the first one left -- is the defect the whole plan is exposed to, and it looks exactly like a tracking gap from one frame. What separates them is distance: a real object that was missed for a frame is found again near where it was, and usually still overlapping its own mask. So each gap is reported with the distance covered per missing frame, the overlap between the mask before the gap and the mask after it, and the distance a continuous object in the same data covers in one frame.
records.context: A recycled id -- the same number given to an unrelated object after the first one left -- is the defect the whole plan is exposed to, and it looks exactly like a tracking gap from one frame. What separates them is distance: a real object that was missed for a frame is found again near where it was, and usually still overlapping its own mask. So each gap is reported with the distance covered per missing frame, the overlap between the mask before the gap and the mask after it, and the distance a continuous object in the same data covers in one frame.
records.translation: Um id reciclado -- o mesmo número dado a um objeto não relacionado depois que o primeiro saiu -- é o defeito ao qual todo o plano está exposto, e ele parece exatamente uma lacuna de rastreamento de um quadro. O que os distingue é a distância: um objeto real que deixou de ser detectado em um quadro é reencontrado perto de onde estava e, em geral, ainda sobrepondo a própria máscara. Por isso, cada lacuna é relatada com a distância percorrida por quadro ausente, a sobreposição entre a máscara antes da lacuna e a máscara depois dela, e a distância que um objeto contínuo nos mesmos dados percorre em um quadro.
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)
